title: William Eustis (Secretary of War) → Gen. James Wilkinson, routine letter with part of the message in cypher
shelfmark: Chicago History Museum, James Wilkinson papers, vol. 3 (Nov 1806-May 1812), page 67, item 93
folio_note: one letter; the calendar says 'part of message in cypher'; extent unknown
status: Calendar entry in the finding aid (p.29 of 49): 'Routine: officer transfers; part of message in cypher'. No decipherment noted. The neighbouring item 91 (4 May 1809, Eustis, 'receipt of ciphered message') is the preceding cipher message. Not on DECODE as far as checked.
why: Wilkinson's cipher traffic with the War Department in the weeks after the Burr trial and before his recall inquiry; the Wilkinson-Spanish dictionary codes are already being studied, this is a US War Department cipher.
verify: Ask CHM Research Center for the item scan / the 1976 microfilm (also holds Kingsbury and Hardin papers); look for a War Department key in the Dearborn/Eustis letterbooks (NARA RG 107)
prior_art: open (checked 28 Oct 2026: web search Wilkinson/Eustis/cipher/CHM; Founders Online; Chu-Valenti-Knight Wilkinson project covers the Spanish codes only)

title: William Eustis (Secretary of War) → Gen. James Wilkinson, letter with 'ciphered message'
shelfmark: Chicago History Museum, James Wilkinson papers, vol. 3, page 66, item 91
folio_note: one letter; calendar: 'receipt of ciphered message'; may only acknowledge a ciphered message
status: Calendar entry: 'Routine; receipt of ciphered message; most necessary for U.S. to maintain friendly relations with neighboring colonies'. Probably a clear acknowledgement, so weaker than item 93. No decipherment noted.
why: Companion to the 10 May 1809 item; context for US policy toward Spanish and British colonies as Wilkinson returned to New Orleans.
verify: Check with CHM whether the item itself carries cipher groups

title: Fragment of a reported conversation avowing allegiance to the U.S. rather than Britain, 'contains numerical cypher notations'
shelfmark: Chicago History Museum, James Wilkinson papers, vol. 4 (May 1812-1823, undated at the end), page 125, item 174
folio_note: one fragment; numerical cypher notations (amount unknown)
status: Calendar entry (undated materials at end of vol. 4): 'Fragment; report of conversation avowing allegiance to U.S. rather than Britain; contains numerical cypher notations'. No decipherment noted.
why: Possible numerical code in the Wilkinson papers; could be a key fragment or an agent's report from the Burr-conspiracy or Louisiana years.
